disposition_reason: Nationwide Peru survey (2018 bean Cd data points, 2051 soil) used to build random-forest predictive maps; the main text prints measured bean Cd summaries only for two Piura irrigation-contrast sites (Las Lomas, La Quemazón). Department-level results are model-predicted proportions of farms in Cd classes (Fig. 8, graphical) and percentage ranges of farms above buyer thresholds, not measured regional statistics; the authors state they cannot share the data.
disposition_locator: Section 2.1 (p.2-4), Section 3 Results (p.5-6), Fig. 8 (p.11), Data availability (p.13)

study.design: farm survey (nationwide, tree-level and farm-composite sampling) with random-forest spatial modelling
study.material_scope: cacao beans (pods harvested, beans oven-dried at 70 C, whole beans ground) and soils 0-20 cm
study.growing_origin_vs_market: grown in Peru: 563 tree-level farms in 35 provinces of 13 departments (Tumbes, Piura, Amazonas, Cajamarca, San Martin, Ucayali, Huanuco, Pasco, Junin, Cusco, Madre de Dios, Ayacucho, plus others; Loreto and Puno appear in Fig. 8) plus 484 farm-composite farms; not market samples
study.collection_period: April 2018 to September 2019 (tree-level sampling); farm-composite sampling period not separately stated
study.sampling_unit: 1534 tree-level bean samples (up to 4 pods per tree, up to 6 trees per farm, 563 farms) + 484 farm-level composite bean samples (5-10 pods, ~1 kg fresh beans per farm)
study.method: Tree-level beans: SENASA ISO-certified lab, 0.5 g digested in 6 ml HNO3 + 2 ml H2O2 at 200 C, ICP-MS. Farm composites: SGS, AOAC Official Method 2013.06 (modified 2019). Soil: SGS aqua regia open block, ICP-MS (Nexion 2000C).
study.lod_loq: Beans (SENASA tree-level): LOQ 0.047 mg/kg. Beans (SGS farm composites): LOD 0.01 mg/kg, LOQ 0.03 mg/kg. Soil: LOQ 0.01 mg/kg.
study.basis: whole beans oven-dried at 70 C for 48 h to ~7% moisture (reported as mg/kg; dry-weight basis not explicitly stated, residual moisture ~7%)
study.qa: Soil: CRM OREAS 906 (0.42 ± 0.04 mg/kg Cd), 5% duplicates, blanks every 50. SENASA: blanks and duplicates every 10 samples, internal bean Cd controls. SGS beans: average recovery 105% (80-110%). Both labs in a 24-lab interlaboratory ring test (z-scores < 2).

findings.material: cacao beans (unfermented beans from harvested pods, oven-dried, ground whole)
findings.group: Las Lomas, Piura (irrigated; upstream active mining)
findings.basis: whole beans oven-dried at 70 C for 48 h to ~7% moisture (reported as mg/kg; dry-weight basis not explicitly stated, residual moisture ~7%)
findings.censoring: not described for this site summary; national protocol analysed remaining trees on a farm only if the first randomly selected tree exceeded bean LOQ 0.047 mg/kg or soil 0.05 mg/kg
findings.locator: Section 3 Results, p.5, paragraph on DGT irrigation water (Las Lomas / La Quemazón)
findings.notes: Among the highest bean Cd in Piura; corresponding soil Cd 2.80 ± 0.82 mg/kg. n of trees/farms not reported. Selected as a high-Cd contrast site, not a random regional sample.

findings.material: cacao beans (unfermented beans from harvested pods, oven-dried, ground whole)
findings.group: La Quemazon, Piura (irrigated; fewer upstream mines)
findings.basis: whole beans oven-dried at 70 C for 48 h to ~7% moisture (reported as mg/kg; dry-weight basis not explicitly stated, residual moisture ~7%)
findings.censoring: not described for this site summary; national protocol analysed remaining trees on a farm only if the first randomly selected tree exceeded bean LOQ 0.047 mg/kg or soil 0.05 mg/kg
findings.locator: Section 3 Results, p.5, paragraph on DGT irrigation water (Las Lomas / La Quemazón)
findings.notes: Among the lowest bean Cd in Piura; corresponding soil Cd 0.54 ± 0.1 mg/kg. n not reported. Authors note Las Lomas bean Cd ten times higher despite only ~4x higher irrigation-water Cd load.

controls.control: Siting / sourcing by geography: avoid or segregate beans from high-Cd departments
controls.comparator: Model-predicted bean Cd across Peruvian departments
controls.outcome: Predicted share of farms potentially impacted (bean Cd above 0.8 / 0.5 mg/kg buyer thresholds): Tumbes 59-89%, Piura 89-100%, Amazonas 51-79%, Loreto 27-95%; nationally 16-45% of cacao farming households and 9.2-41% of national production. Fig. 8 (graphical) shows southern departments (Cusco, Ayacucho, Junin, Puno) almost entirely in the <0.5 mg/kg predicted class. These are random-forest predictions (bean model spatial-block CV R2 0.48 ± 0.26), not measured means.
controls.locator: Section 3 Results p.6; Fig. 8 p.11; Abstract

controls.control: Irrigation water source (upstream mining vs fewer mines)
controls.comparator: Las Lomas canal (active mining upstream) vs La Quemazon canal (fewer mines, different bedrock), DGT membranes monthly for one year (12 per site)
controls.outcome: Labile Cd in irrigation water 0.315 ± 0.267 ug/L (Las Lomas) vs 0.085 ± 0.108 ug/L (La Quemazon); estimated bioavailable Cd influx 3.15 ± 2.67 vs 0.85 ± 1.08 mg per tree per year; bean Cd 7.12 ± 2.70 vs 0.72 ± 0.36 mg/kg. Two sites only; soil Cd also differed (2.80 vs 0.54 mg/kg), so water is not isolated as the cause.
controls.locator: Section 2.1 p.4; Section 3 p.5-6; Section 4.2 p.12

controls.comparator: Alluvial-plain farms flooded at least once a decade vs hillside farms, Santiago River watershed, Amazonas
controls.outcome: 3.5-fold difference in Cd translocation factor (bean Cd / soil Cd); absolute bean values not reported. Nationally bean Cd tended to be higher near lakes/rivers, under alluvial flooding and on fluvial deposits, and near active mining (Piura-Tumbes; San Martin-Huanuco-Ucayali-Pasco).

controls.comparator: Partial dependence of bean Cd on soil pH in nationwide random-forest model
controls.outcome: Soil pH related positively to soil Cd but negatively to bean Cd (higher Cd solubility/translocation in acidic soils); no numeric effect size printed. Not an intervention test.

controls.control: Blending beans from high- and low-Cd areas (bulk market)
controls.outcome: Authors assume Huanuco farmers report no Cd-related losses because buyers mix beans from alluvial high-Cd farms with beans from further from the river; no measured blend values.

In Peru buyers typically use 0.5 mg/kg for bulk beans and 0.8 to 1.2 mg/kg for single-origin fine-flavour beans; 0.6 mg/kg cited as unofficial importer threshold; some buyers request as low as 0.3 mg/kg. Piura farmers reported average income losses of 31% (Villar et al. 2022, cited).
controls.locator: Section 2.4 p.5; Section 4.3 p.12; Section 1 p.2

regulatory.product: chocolate and cocoa derivatives (source states existing limits range 0.3 to 0.8 mg/kg depending on product; individual values not itemised)

regulatory.instrument: FSANZ Standard 1.4.1; Indonesian National Standard; SanPin 2.3.2-1078-01

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Summary reports 'irrigation water Cd ... Las Lomas 2.80 ± 0.82 mg/m3 (soil Cd sites), 7.12 ± 2.70 mg/m3 (bean Cd sites)'; primary: 2.80 ± 0.82 and 7.12 ± 2.70 mg/kg are soil and bean Cd at Las Lomas; irrigation water was 0.315 ± 0.267 ug/L (Las Lomas) and 0.085 ± 0.108 ug/L (La Quemazon). Summary also omits La Quemazon bean Cd 0.72 ± 0.36 mg/kg.
Summary says 'Farm-level bean analysis: SENASA'; primary: SENASA analysed tree-level beans (LOQ 0.047), SGS analysed farm-level composites (LOD 0.01, LOQ 0.03).
Summary lists aqua regia digestion alongside bean method; aqua regia was for soil; beans were HNO3/H2O2.
Summary says '100-150 farms targeted per region'; primary says 100-150 cacao trees per region.

Summary states 'EU regulatory thresholds for cacao: 0.6 mg/kg (cacao powder), 0.8 mg/kg (cacao beans) per EC 488/2014'; primary does not state this; it cites 0.6 mg/kg as an unofficial importer threshold and says limits range 0.3-0.8 mg/kg depending on product.
Summary gives sample_n 2194 (trees); bean data points were 2018 (1534 tree-level + 484 composites); 2194 trees were selected/sampled.
Summary says '<20% of farms nationally affected'; the Results give 16-45% of households (0.8 vs 0.5 mg/kg thresholds); the <20% figure appears only in the abstract/highlights.
Summary says regional block CV R2 0.36-0.87; primary: regional R2 ranged 0.36-0.87 for soil and 0.22-0.85 for bean models.
Summary says Las Lomas irrigation Cd highest in 'dry season'; primary says June-October (Las Lomas) and May-June (La Quemazon).
unresolved: Measured bean Cd summaries by department/region (means, medians, ranges, n) are not printed in the main text; Supplementary material (Figs S1-S27, Suppl. 1) was not available in the library and the authors state they cannot share data.
Fig. 8 department proportions are model predictions shown only graphically; not transcribed as numbers.
n of trees/farms behind the Las Lomas and La Quemazon means not reported.
Internal inconsistency: abstract says <20% of households nationally impacted; Results say 16-45% depending on threshold.
Whether the 70 C oven-dried beans (~7% moisture) are reported on a dry-weight or as-dried basis is not stated.
